## The question

[Reciproque version of TAF](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2451942/reciproque-version-of-taf), asked by [Houssaine Philou](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/449648/houssaine-philou) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2017-09-30; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Is the following statement true ?
>
> Let $a,b \in \mathbb{R}$ and $f$ a real-valued continous function on $[a,b$]. Do we have the following statement: for every $c\in ]a,b[$ there exist a derivable fucntion $\varphi$ on $]a,b[$  such that
> $$\varphi(a) - \varphi(b) = f(c)(a-b).$$
>
> If yes, how can we get it. Thank you
:::

Sure.  Let $\phi(x) = f(c) x$.
